# The Slow Work of Extraction

## Scripture

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law.” — Galatians 5:22–23

## Reflection

Good pour-over coffee cannot be rushed. Pour the water too fast and it channels straight through the grounds, leaving a thin, sour cup. The best flavor comes from a slow, steady pour—water resting on the grounds, coaxing out what's hidden inside. Extraction takes time. So does fruit.

Paul lists the fruit of the Spirit as a single harvest, not a vending-machine selection. We don't grit our teeth and manufacture patience by Friday; the Spirit grows it in us the way hot water draws sweetness from roasted beans—gradually, under steady attention. That means the frustrating coworker, the interrupted morning, the prayer that seems unanswered are not obstacles to your spiritual life. They are the pour. They are the conditions God is using to extract something you couldn't produce on your own.

Here's the practical comfort: you are not the barista of your own sanctification. Your job is not to force the flavor out but to stay under the water—remain in Scripture, in prayer, in community—and let the Spirit do the work. Some mornings the cup tastes bitter and you wonder if anything is happening. Keep pouring. The Roaster knows the bean He's working with, and He isn't finished. Fruit ripens slowly, but it ripens surely.

## Prayer

Father, we confess our impatience with Your slow work in us. Keep us under Your Word and Spirit, trusting You to grow love, joy, and peace in Your time. Form Christ in us, even through the mornings we don't understand. Amen.

## One-Line Application

Stay under the pour today; let the Spirit do the extracting.
